proposed_widenings.name: ObjectMaterial.stone
proposed_widenings.justification: Stone Shape targets a stone object or section of stone. The ObjectFilter.material field only accepts 'metal' | 'flammable'; 'stone' is absent from OBJECT_MATERIALS.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You touch a stone object of Medium size or smaller or a section of stone no more than 5 feet in any dimension

proposed_widenings.name: reshape_object
proposed_widenings.justification: Stone Shape transforms an existing stone object into an arbitrary player-defined form at cast time. alter_item_kind requires a fixed authored newKind string (a pre-specified destination form like 'rowboat'). Stone Shape's destination is open-ended — the player chooses any shape — so no closed newKind value can be authored. A new atom is needed for open-ended material reshaping of an existing object, distinct from alter_item_kind (fixed destination) and create_object (creates new matter from nothing).
proposed_widenings.evidence: form it into any shape you like. For example, you could shape a large rock into a weapon, statue, or coffer, or you could make a small passage through a wall that is 5 feet thick. You could also shape a stone door or its frame to seal the door shut.

notes: Two independent gaps block encoding. First: ObjectMaterial needs 'stone' added (surface_widening). Second and primary: no atom exists for open-ended object reshaping where the destination form is player-defined at cast time rather than pre-authored. alter_item_kind is semantically wrong (it encodes a fixed known destination, e.g., Folding Boat's box/rowboat/keelboat states); create_object creates new matter rather than reshaping existing stone. The proposed reshape_object atom would carry the existing attachment (Attachment.object) and accept an open-ended player-described target shape, with mechanical constraints (maxHinges, noFinerDetail) as optional metadata. The spell's secondary mechanical effects (passage through wall, sealed door) are DM-adjudicated consequences of the physical change, not additional atoms.
